source.title: Exploring the Effect of Multi-Step Ascent in Sharpness-Aware Minimization
source.authors: Hoki Kim; Jinseong Park; Woo-Jin Lee; Jaewook Lee; Yu-Jin Choi

record.file_problem: The supplied text is complete. Some table columns are flattened, so only clearly attributable values are extracted.
record.tranche_reason: Compares generalization performance across SAM variants and measures loss-landscape properties using a different method from the claim versions. The reported results do not measure the specific behaviors named by V1–V8.
record.gate_note: Reports test accuracy for SAM and other optimizer variants, and measures perturbed losses, gradient similarities and Hessian spectra. The cited prior findings in the introduction are not extracted as this study's results. Some accuracy table columns are flattened; only clearly attributable results are included.
record.test_reason: The study uses the sharpness–generalization rationale to analyze and improve SAM. Its optimizer accuracy comparisons, perturbed losses and Hessian spectra do not test any supplied version. In particular, it does not measure magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance against training-to-test gaps (V7). ASAM is not an Adam-versus-SGD comparison (V4).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: ascent-step count changes perturbed weights, gradients and final loss landscapes, and the proposed intermediate-gradient modification improves multi-step SAM's test accuracy in the reported experiments.
record.recipe_differences: Studies multi-step ascent within sharpness-aware minimization and proposes an update using gradients at intermediate perturbed weights; it does not test the mapped claim recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The number of ascent steps changes perturbed losses and gradients. The authors report that SAM performance rarely changes with N, while MSAM improves over SAM for N ≥ 3; MSAM performance is stable across tested step-size ratios and across the reported rho sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: MSAM-2 improves reported test accuracy over SAM-2: 96.88 versus 96.58 on CIFAR-10, 85.87 versus 84.91 on CIFAR-100 under Acc(A), and 77.9 versus 77.1 on ImageNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Using intermediate perturbed-weight gradients can improve multi-step SAM's test accuracy in these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: More ascent steps yield higher directional perturbed losses and different gradients; MSAM-2 has a lower maximum Hessian eigenvalue than SAM-1 and SAM-2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ascent-step count and intermediate-gradient updates affect SAM's optimization diagnostics and loss-landscape geometry.

record.problems: The accuracy comparisons do not report training accuracy, so the training-to-test gap cannot be assessed. ImageNet comparator values for ESAM, GSAM and ASAM are referred to their respective papers. The sharpness results are primarily described qualitatively, and the Hessian comparison does not establish a relationship between sharpness and the training-to-test gap.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results omitted. Table 2 and Table 3 contain flattened Acc(B), Reported and Best columns; those values are not separately extracted where the flattened text does not support reliable assignment.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label and random-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its ranking of training-to-test gaps among comparably fitted networks, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: No supplied version receives a verdict. Table 1 also reports training and perturbed losses, but these do not establish V7's specified measure or generalization-gap relationship. No additional version-bearing results are missing.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and their local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Large versus small batch sizes and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their effects across training-set sizes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, comparisons at similarly low training loss, and whether the measure ranks training-to-test gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measured perturbed loss along ascent directions as the number of ascent steps varied.
rows.value: Loss value increases as N increases for all k; perturbed loss with v10 is significantly higher than that of v1.
rows.note: This is a loss-landscape observation, not a training-to-test gap measurement.
rows.check: Measures directional perturbed training loss, without magnitude scaling or a comparison against generalization gaps; it cannot establish V7.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine similarities between gradients at perturbed weights for different ascent-step counts.
rows.value: Similarity between ∇`(wp1)` and ∇`(wp2)` is 0.93; between ∇`(wp1)` and ∇`(wp4)` is 0.88.
rows.note: The authors also state that cosine similarity between ∇`(w)` and ∇`(wpN)` decreases as N increases.
rows.check: Gradient cosine similarity is an optimization diagnostic, not a measure named by any supplied version.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Measured Hessian spectra for models trained with SAM-1, SAM-2 and MSAM-2.
rows.measure: Hessian eigenvalue spectrum and maximum eigenvalue
rows.value: MSAM has the smallest curvature and the lowest maximum eigenvalue and spectrum of the Hessian compared to SAM-1 and SAM-2.
rows.note: The text gives no numerical eigenvalues and does not report a training-to-test gap for these models.
rows.check: The qualitative ordering is correct, but Figure 10 supplies numerical maximum eigenvalues: SAM-1 13.60, SAM-2 11.89, MSAM-2 3.96. The note claiming no numerical eigenvalues is wrong. Hessian curvature does not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its association with generalization gaps.
